hero.headline: St. Lucie Nuclear Power Plant Unit 1 manually shut down after control rods drop into reactor core
hero.teaser: St. Lucie Nuclear Power Plant Unit 1 was manually shut down Wednesday morning after three control rods dropped into the reactor core, according to a notification filed with the Nuc
hero.body:
St. Lucie Nuclear Power Plant Unit 1 was manually shut down Wednesday morning after three control rods dropped into the reactor core, according to a notification filed with the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. The manual reactor trip occurred at 9:47 a.m. on August 13, 2026, while Unit 1 was operating at 100 percent power. The NRC classified the event as a non-emergency.

The trip was uncomplicated with all systems responding normally after the shutdown, according to the licensee. Operations stabilized the plant in Mode 3, known as Hot Standby. Decay heat is being removed by discharging steam to the main condenser using the turbine bypass valves and main feedwater.

Unit 2 at the Saint Lucie facility was not affected by the incident. According to the NRC website, Unit 1 remains shut down.

The licensee reported that at the time of the manual trip, the reactor was in Mode 1 at 100 percent power. All systems responded normally following the shutdown procedure, and operations successfully stabilized the plant.

Drivers across the Treasure Coast should prepare for a busy week of road construction, overnight lane closures and I-95 ramp shutdowns in Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties.

- Two southbound I-95 lanes between Glades Cut Off Road and just south of Okeechobee Road in St. Lucie County may be closed from 9 p.m. Friday, Aug. 14, until 6 a.m. Monday, Aug. 17, for milling and repaving.
- Multiple I-95 ramps at Kanner Highway and High Meadow Avenue in Martin County are scheduled for overnight closures from Sunday, Aug. 16, through Friday, Aug. 21.
- All four I-95 ramps at Midway Road in St. Lucie County are scheduled for overnight closures during the same period, with only one ramp closed at a time.
- Several side streets along the SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard widening project may close for extended periods between Monday morning and Friday afternoon.
- I-95 will have recurring nighttime lane closures near Gatlin Boulevard, Becker Road, Oslo Road and other active construction zones.

FDOT is also giving advance notice that the northbound I-95 exit to High Meadow Avenue is scheduled to close from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Thursday, Aug. 27, for overhead sign installation.

Two-way traffic will be maintained by flaggers.

**Southbound I-95 exit to Midway Road:** Drivers will continue to the St. Lucie West Boulevard exit, head east and enter northbound I-95 to return to the Midway Road exit.

The weather contingency period is Aug. 23 through Aug. 28.

### I-95 between Gatlin Boulevard and Becker Road

Northbound and southbound I-95 between Gatlin Boulevard and just south of Becker Road will have two lanes closed, with possible lane shifts, from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, Aug. 16, through Friday, Aug. 21, for milling and repaving.

FDOT is also advising drivers that the southbound I-95 entrance ramp from Gatlin Boulevard/Tradition Parkway is scheduled to close overnight Aug. 26 and Aug. 27.

### Port St. Lucie Boulevard and U.S. 1

One lane on SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard may close intermittently from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday, Aug. 17, through Friday, Aug. 21.

Drivers on A1A/Jimmy Buffett Memorial Highway near Sebastian Inlet State Park may encounter one northbound or southbound lane or shoulder closure as needed during daytime construction work.

Only one lane will be closed at a time, with flaggers directing traffic through the work zone.

Sections of the north and south parking lots at Sebastian Inlet State Park also remain partially closed around the clock for bridge construction. The park remains open, but parking is limited in affected areas.

Construction schedules can change because of weather, emergencies or other conditions.

Drivers can check around-the-clock I-95 traffic conditions through [FL511](https://fl511.com/) and should watch for posted detour signs near active ramp and road closures.

cards.headline: Palm City woman held on $275,000 bond after 36 Border Collies rescued from Southwest Alligator Street home
cards.teaser: Paige Anne ODonnell, 62, faces 36 felony counts after Martin County deputies and Animal Services removed 36 Border Collies from her Palm City home where they were living in deplorable conditions with feces and urine-soaked materials throughout the residence.
cards.body:
Paige Anne ODonnell, 62, of the 1200 block of Southwest Alligator Street in Palm City remains in the Martin County Jail on a $275,000 bond following her arrest on Aug. 10 after deputies and Animal Services Unit employees confiscated 36 Border Collies from her home. ODonnell faces 36 third-degree felony counts of torture involving pain, serious physical injury or death, and 36 first-degree misdemeanor counts of keeping animals in an enclosure without exercise and air.

Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said the conditions inside the home were so deplorable that deputies and Animal Services officers had to wear Tyvek protective clothing while working inside. Feces, urine-soaked materials, boxes, and debris throughout the residence made the process of locating and safely removing the animals extremely challenging. An inoperable air-conditioning system demonstrated that the animals had been maintained in conditions that subjected them to unnecessary suffering, according to an arrest affidavit.

During her first appearance in court on Aug. 11, a judge ordered that ODonnell may not own or possess, either temporarily or permanently, any animals as a condition of the bond. The investigation actually began in 2020, and throughout that time ODonnell claimed she had no more than five dogs inside the home. All the animals were turned over to the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast in Palm City where they are being evaluated, cleaned, treated, and cared for. The Humane Society is asking for public donations towards the care of the 36 dogs.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast traffic report: I-95 ramp closures, road work planned Aug. 14-21
cards.teaser: Drivers across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties should prepare for overnight I-95 ramp closures, weekend lane restrictions and local road closures through Aug. 21, including work at Kanner Highway, High Meadow Avenue and Midway Road.
cards.body:
Drivers across the Treasure Coast should prepare for a busy week of road construction, overnight lane closures and I-95 ramp shutdowns in Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties.

The Florida Department of Transportation's traffic report for Aug. 14 through Aug. 21 includes multiple overnight ramp closures along I-95, a weekend-long lane restriction near Fort Pierce, extended local street closures in Port St. Lucie and continued work on several major bridge and widening projects.

## Biggest traffic impacts this week

Among the most significant impacts for Treasure Coast drivers:

- Two southbound I-95 lanes between Glades Cut Off Road and just south of Okeechobee Road in St. Lucie County may be closed from 9 p.m. Friday, Aug. 14, until 6 a.m. Monday, Aug. 17, for milling and repaving.
- Multiple I-95 ramps at Kanner Highway and High Meadow Avenue in Martin County are scheduled for overnight closures from Sunday, Aug. 16, through Friday, Aug. 21.
- All four I-95 ramps at Midway Road in St. Lucie County are scheduled for overnight closures during the same period, with only one ramp closed at a time.
- Several side streets along the SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard widening project may close for extended periods between Monday morning and Friday afternoon.
- I-95 will have recurring nighttime lane closures near Gatlin Boulevard, Becker Road, Oslo Road and other active construction zones.

FDOT schedules can change because of weather or other unforeseen conditions. Drivers should allow extra travel time and use caution in work zones.

## Martin County

### I-95 ramp closures at Kanner Highway and High Meadow Avenue

The largest Martin County impacts are tied to the $40.8 million I-95 resurfacing project between the Bridge Road area and the Martin-St. Lucie county line.

Southbound I-95 between Kanner Highway, Exit 101, and Bridge Road, Exit 96, will have two lanes closed from 4 p.m. to 5:30 a.m. Monday, Aug. 17, through Thursday, Aug. 20.

Farther south, both directions of I-95 between Bridge Road and the Martin-St. Lucie county line will also have two lanes closed overnight. Southbound closures are scheduled from 7:30 p.m. to 5:30 a.m., while northbound closures are scheduled from 8:30 p.m. to 6:30 a.m., Sunday through Friday.

Several ramps will close overnight from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, Aug. 16, through Friday, Aug. 21. FDOT says only one ramp will be closed at a time.

**Southbound I-95 exit to Kanner Highway:** Drivers will continue south to Bridge Road, Exit 96, head east on Bridge Road and use the northbound I-95 entrance ramp to return to Kanner Highway.

**Southbound I-95 entrance from Kanner Highway:** Drivers will be directed west on Kanner Highway, east on Pratt Whitney Road, south on Pratt Whitney Road and east on Bridge Road to the southbound I-95 entrance ramp.

**Southbound I-95 exit to High Meadow Avenue:** Drivers will continue south to Kanner Highway, head east on Kanner Highway and use northbound I-95 to reach the High Meadow Avenue exit.

**Southbound I-95 entrance from High Meadow Avenue:** Drivers will be detoured north on High Meadow Avenue, east on Martin Highway and south on Kanner Highway to the southbound I-95 entrance ramp.

Weather contingency dates for those closures are Aug. 23 through Aug. 28.

FDOT is also giving advance notice that the northbound I-95 exit to High Meadow Avenue is scheduled to close from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Thursday, Aug. 27, for overhead sign installation.

### U.S. 1 in Stuart

Northbound and southbound U.S. 1 between north of SE Fischer Street and north of SE Decker Avenue may have two lanes closed intermittently from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, Aug. 16, through Friday, Aug. 21, for sign installation.

The work is part of a $7.5 million resurfacing and safety project that includes wider bicycle lanes, new LED lighting, pedestrian signal upgrades and sidewalk-ramp improvements.

### A1A near Jensen Beach Causeway

One lane of northbound or southbound A1A/NE Ocean Boulevard between NE Shore Village Terrace and south of the Jensen Beach Causeway may close intermittently Monday, Aug. 17, through Friday, Aug. 21, for pavement widening and drainage work.

Two-way traffic will be maintained by flaggers.

### Martin Highway in Palm City

Eastbound and westbound Martin Highway between east of SW Stuart West Boulevard and west of Citrus Boulevard may have one lane closed intermittently from 7 p.m. to 6 a.m. Tuesday, Aug. 18, through Thursday, Aug. 20, for milling and resurfacing.

Additional daytime utility work is planned in Palm City and Stuart, including intermittent lane closures on Martin Highway and U.S. 1.

## St. Lucie County

### Weekend I-95 lane restrictions near Fort Pierce

Southbound I-95 between Glades Cut Off Road and just south of Okeechobee Road may have two lanes closed beginning at 9 p.m. Friday, Aug. 14, with lanes reopening by 6 a.m. Monday, Aug. 17, as needed for milling and repaving.

The same stretch of I-95 will have additional overnight lane and shoulder closures Sunday, Aug. 16, through Friday, Aug. 21.

### Midway Road I-95 ramp closures

Each of the four I-95 ramps at Midway Road is scheduled for an overnight closure from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, Aug. 16, through Friday, Aug. 21. FDOT says only one ramp closure will occur at a time.

**Northbound I-95 entrance from Midway Road:** Drivers will be directed to southbound I-95, exit at St. Lucie West Boulevard, head east and use the northbound I-95 entrance ramp.

**Northbound I-95 exit to Midway Road:** Drivers will use the St. Lucie West Boulevard exit, continue east on St. Lucie West Boulevard/SW Prima Vista Boulevard and travel north on U.S. 1 to Midway Road.

**Southbound I-95 exit to Midway Road:** Drivers will continue to the St. Lucie West Boulevard exit, head east and enter northbound I-95 to return to the Midway Road exit.

**Southbound I-95 entrance from Midway Road:** Drivers will travel east on Midway Road, south on U.S. 1 and west on St. Lucie West Boulevard/SW Prima Vista Boulevard to reach the southbound I-95 entrance ramp.

The weather contingency period is Aug. 23 through Aug. 28.

### I-95 between Gatlin Boulevard and Becker Road

Northbound and southbound I-95 between Gatlin Boulevard and just south of Becker Road will have two lanes closed, with possible lane shifts, from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, Aug. 16, through Friday, Aug. 21, for milling and repaving.

FDOT is also advising drivers that the southbound I-95 entrance ramp from Gatlin Boulevard/Tradition Parkway is scheduled to close overnight Aug. 26 and Aug. 27.

### Port St. Lucie Boulevard and U.S. 1

Drivers should expect daytime and nighttime lane closures along Port St. Lucie Boulevard and U.S. 1 as part of a $6.8 million resurfacing and safety project.

Port St. Lucie Boulevard between SE Seafury Lane and SE Lennard Road may have one lane closed from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday and two lanes closed intermittently from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday through Friday.

U.S. 1 between SE Jennings Road and NW Golden Oak Trail may also have one lane closed during both daytime and overnight work periods.

### Extended closures along SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard

The SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard widening project will continue to affect local roads between SW Jordin Avenue and SW Alcantarra Boulevard.

One lane on SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard may close intermittently from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday, Aug. 17, through Friday, Aug. 21.

FDOT also says extended closures may occur on SW Jaslo Avenue, SW Jacoby Avenue, SW McCullough Avenue, SW McCall Road, SW McHord Avenue and SW Paar Drive while crews install drainage and utilities.

Those closures may begin at 7 a.m. Monday and continue until 5 p.m. Friday. Adjacent roads will not be closed at the same time, and access to homes and businesses will be maintained.

### North Causeway Bridge area

The new A1A North Causeway Bridge opened to traffic in May, but construction continues around the project.

U.S. 1 between the Juanita Avenue intersection and Naco Road may have one northbound lane closed from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. weekdays through September.

Additional lane closures continue on Juanita Avenue, Harbortown Drive, Old Dixie Highway and other roads around the bridge construction area.

For boaters, FDOT says intermittent full channel closures may occur for up to six hours between dawn and dusk on weekdays through September while crews remove steel bascule bridge spans. Vessels requiring full channel access must provide the bridge tender with 120 minutes of advance notice.

## Indian River County

### 17th Street Bridge in Vero Beach

One lane on the eastbound or westbound 17th Street bridges between Indian River Boulevard and Indian Bay Drive may remain closed through late summer as crews complete striping and other work.

The closed lane may shift between the inside and outside travel lanes as needed.

### I-95 and Oslo Road interchange

Construction continues on the $95.78 million new I-95 interchange and Oslo Road widening project.

I-95 may have one lane closed in either direction from 9 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday through Thursday through August for bridge work. Up to two lanes may close during the same overnight period for milling and resurfacing.

Traffic on Oslo Road remains shifted between the I-95 bridge area and SW 58th Avenue, with one westbound lane and one eastbound lane open.

### 85th Street widening project

Northbound and southbound S.R. 510/90th Avenue between Sebastian Boulevard and 87th Street may have one lane closed intermittently from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, Aug. 16, through Friday, Aug. 21, for roadway construction.

### Sebastian Inlet Bridge construction

Drivers on A1A/Jimmy Buffett Memorial Highway near Sebastian Inlet State Park may encounter one northbound or southbound lane or shoulder closure as needed during daytime construction work.

Only one lane will be closed at a time, with flaggers directing traffic through the work zone.

Sections of the north and south parking lots at Sebastian Inlet State Park also remain partially closed around the clock for bridge construction. The park remains open, but parking is limited in affected areas.

## Check conditions before leaving

Construction schedules can change because of weather, emergencies or other conditions.

Drivers can check around-the-clock I-95 traffic conditions through [FL511](https://fl511.com/) and should watch for posted detour signs near active ramp and road closures.

hero.headline: St. Lucie Nuclear Power Plant Unit 1 manually shut down after control rods drop into reactor core
hero.teaser: St. Lucie Nuclear Power Plant Unit 1 was manually shut down Wednesday morning after three control rods dropped into the reactor core, according to a notification filed with the Nuc
hero.body:
St. Lucie Nuclear Power Plant Unit 1 was manually shut down Wednesday morning after three control rods dropped into the reactor core, according to a notification filed with the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. The manual reactor trip occurred at 9:47 a.m. on August 13, 2026, while Unit 1 was operating at 100 percent power. The NRC classified the event as a non-emergency.

The trip was uncomplicated with all systems responding normally after the shutdown, according to the licensee. Operations stabilized the plant in Mode 3, known as Hot Standby. Decay heat is being removed by discharging steam to the main condenser using the turbine bypass valves and main feedwater.

Unit 2 at the Saint Lucie facility was not affected by the incident. According to the NRC website, Unit 1 remains shut down.

The licensee reported that at the time of the manual trip, the reactor was in Mode 1 at 100 percent power. All systems responded normally following the shutdown procedure, and operations successfully stabilized the plant.
